precepts.text: For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh. Why had they not seen Paul's face? Because he never went to Laodicea and he never went to Colosse.
precepts.point: Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world. On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it, and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities in that region. The word spread throughout those cities. You read about Laodicea in Revelation.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Paul writes “To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse,” just as Ephesians is written to the saints at Ephesus. Same concept: these are Israelites in Asia. Then he says, “Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus.” What is Paul saying? He never went to Colosse. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that it spread all throughout Asia, and Paul heard there was another congregation over in Colosse that was fervent in spirit too, so he wrote to them.

Chapter 2 proves it: “For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Why had they not seen Paul’s face? Because he never went to Laodicea, and he never went to Colosse. For anyone who wondered why there is no precept in Acts of Paul going to Colosse, that is the precept.

On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it (the Laodicea you read about in Revelation), and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities of that region. The gospel spread through all those cities, “as it is in all the world.” Acts 19 says Paul turned away much people “not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia” from the goddess Diana, the woman all Asia worshipped, just as America worships the Virgin Mary. The spirit was so heavy on the apostle that places he never physically went to were getting touched.

precepts.text: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, always labouring fervently for you in prayers; for I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis. So his companion in the truth and the gospel, his fellow soldier Epaphras, was of Laodicea and was going back and forth, dealing with Laodicea directly.
precepts.point: Paul had a group of fellow soldiers that were about the work, not being pressured. They were about God's business.
precepts.why:
Paul writes of the great conflict he has “for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Laodicea is in Asia Minor. When you read the book of Acts, it is not written specifically that Paul went to Laodicea. He did go to Asia Minor, but it does not say he went to Laodicea. They had not seen his face in the flesh. One of his companions did go.

“Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” His companion in the truth and the gospel, his fellow soldier Epaphras, was of that region, going back and forth, and he was the one dealing with Laodicea directly.

On the map of Asia Minor you see Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Smyrna, Philadelphia, Ephesus and Laodicea, with a river that splits between Ephesus, Philadelphia and Laodicea. Paul had a group of fellow soldiers like Epaphras who were about the work without being pressured. They were about God’s business, labouring fervently in prayer that the brethren would stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.

precepts.text: So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Knit together as one man, one mind. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.
precepts.why:
Paul prays “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love”. That is how all of us ought to be: our hearts and our minds knit together. Judges shows what that looks like: “So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.” Knit together as one man, one mind.

In this truth we have to learn to work together. All nations do it. Chinese work together with Chinese, East Indians with East Indians, Arabs with Arabs, white folks with white folks. It's only dumb blacks and Latinos that cannot get it together, mainly black people, always with an issue, always with a problem. You can get mad if you want; you know it's true.

That is why we don't have a community. Look at the Chinese community: they have Chinese hospitals, Chinese supermarkets, Chinese banks in Chinatown. In the black community we have to go to the white communities for hospitals and grocery stores, which we don't own, and there ain't no black banks around here. So when we say we have a community, we are lying to ourselves and lying to the people. It's just BS.

Israel once gathered as one man. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man again, and that is the knitting together in love that Colossians is speaking of.

precepts.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. That is our hearts being knit together as one man. Honor is a word we have never been taught as a race, as a people. Definition read in class: honor refers to the moral principle of integrity, fairness, and respectability; the term encompasses both a personal ethos and the public esteem in which a person is held; character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty, and a guiding code of conduct. We try to teach the commandments as a guiding code of conduct, and they call it hate speech. In honour preferring one another: you will hear our people say they prefer another race over their own, because we have never learned honor. Story told in class: a store owner shot a young black boy in the back and got off, and our people went right back to shop at those stores. That is preferring other races to your own race.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.
precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love”: that is our hearts being knit together as one man. Then: “in honour preferring one another”. That right there is our problem.

Carter G. Woodson told it: a black store sells ice, and a white man opens an ice store right next door. Guess where black people go to buy ice? The white man's, because they say the white man's ice is colder. In Chicago it's the same with the barber shops: I'm going to the Chinese barber shop because they give better haircuts. You hear black women and black men say, I prefer the white man, I prefer being with the white woman. Why? Because we have never learned honor.

Ask black men and women to explain honor and you get the pimps and the hoochie mamas trying to explain it; they have no honor. We have never been taught honor as a race, as a people. Honor refers to the moral principle of integrity, fairness and respectability; it takes in both a personal ethos and the public esteem in which a person is held: character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty, and a guiding code of conduct. Blacks and Latinos do not understand high moral standards: why can't I show my cleavage, my stomach, the crack of my booty? We try to teach the commandments as a guiding code of conduct, why cover up, why put down the guns, and they call it hate speech. They only do that with our race.

The law says, “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”. The children of your people are the children of your race, not the Chinese, not the white man, not the Arabs. Yet we will love any other race before we love each other. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him; they said he had a gun and found no gun, and he got off. And our people went right back to shop at the Chinese stores, as long as they could get the fake hair, the press-on nails and the makeup. That is preferring other races to your own race, when God says, in honour prefer one another.

precepts.text: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. Now we understand the context of love in the Bible: walking after God's commandments.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.
precepts.why:
Some of you may be new, so understand what “knit together in love” means. It is not talking about rubbing each other's back. It is not talking about putting lotion on each other's feet. John defines it: “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.”

Now we understand the context of love in the Bible: walking after God's commandments. That is the love that knits us together as one man, the same love as being kindly affectioned one to another and in honour preferring one another.

So read Colossians again with that understanding: “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ”. Our hearts are knit together when we keep God's commandments together, and that brings us to the riches of the full assurance of understanding and the mystery of God, which goes back to the chapter before.

precepts.text: That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God: the power of God is the word of God. We do not speak the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought; the princes of this world are the nations. We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory. What we are saying seems so unheard of: it is only for the Israelites, Christ is black, it is about gathering the twelve tribes back together. It is hidden. Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. If the scribes and Pharisees had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right; but they followed Rome. Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him: what God has prepared is unimaginable.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
In the Father and in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul explains that hidden wisdom to the Corinthians: “That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.” Do not let your faith stand in the wisdom of men, the ones who speak very well with six syllable words, quoting poets and philosophers. The power of God is the word of God.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought.” The wisdom of this world says, give us reparations and it will solve all our problems; a lot of black people have hit the lotto and accomplished zero. The princes of this world are the nations.

“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory.” The world does not know it, so what we are saying seems unheard of: it is only for the Israelites? Christ is black and you are going to rule the world? It is about gathering the twelve tribes back together? It is hidden, and it was ordained before the world for our glory.

“Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome. If they had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right.

“But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Brothers and sisters in AI create beautiful things, but what God has prepared no one has ever seen or heard of; it is unimaginable. “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. That is the treasure hid in Christ.

precepts.text: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation. They feared Rome; the princes of the world feared Rome. That was their god.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
Paul says the princes of this world did not know the hidden wisdom, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” John shows why: “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

If they left him alone, everybody was going to believe on him. But they feared Rome. The princes of the world feared Rome, and that was their god. They could see the miracles and still chose their place and their nation under Rome over the Son of God.

That is why the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid from such men. The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome; had they followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right. But they said, no, we follow Rome, and so they crucified the Lord of glory.

precepts.text: Christ said to the Pharisees, ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do; he was talking about Rome, and they obeyed Rome. He was a murderer from the beginning: that goes back to Cain, that hateful spirit, that abode not in the truth.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
This is what Christ said to the Pharisees who followed Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The devil he was talking about was Rome. All the desires of Satan, their father Rome, they would do; they obeyed Rome.

“He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him.” That goes back to Cain, that hateful spirit. Cain did not abide in the truth, and the Pharisees followed that same spirit. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

So the princes of this world could not know the hidden wisdom of God that is in Christ. They were of their father the devil, with no truth in them, and that is why they did not know the Lord of glory and crucified him.

precepts.text: Like as thou canst do none of these things that I have spoken of, even so canst thou not find out my judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised unto my people. Meaning it is unimaginable. We think we can imagine it, but we cannot.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
Paul wrote, “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Ezra was told the same: “Like as thou canst do none of these things that I have spoken of, even so canst thou not find out my judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised unto my people.”

Even so canst thou not find out my judgment, what the Lord is going to do, nor the love He has promised to His people in the end. It is unimaginable. We think we can imagine it, but we cannot. Men can create beautiful things, but nothing like what God has prepared.

That is part of what it means that in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” The things God has prepared for His people are hidden from the heart of man, and only revealed by His Spirit.

precepts.text: This is where Paul was quoting from. Many of the things Paul is saying, he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
When Paul says, “But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him,” where was he quoting from? Isaiah: “For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him.”

Many of the things Paul is saying he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air; he is speaking from a scriptural context. Then he goes on: “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.”

So the hidden wisdom Paul preached, the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hid in Christ, is the same thing the prophets wrote. What God has prepared no one but God has seen, and He reveals it to His people who wait for Him.

precepts.text: My speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, because man's wisdom can beguile you, deceive you.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
Paul warns “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.” To beguile is to charm, enchant or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or cunning way; the word bridges a line between friendly charm and sneaky manipulation.

What are those enticing words? They go back to the wisdom of this world. Paul says of himself: “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”. Why? Because man's wisdom can beguile you and deceive you.

Paul was not pulling things out of thin air. What he taught he got from the scriptures, the Old Testament, and “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. So the preaching that does not beguile is the word revealed by the spirit, not the enticing words of man's wisdom.

precepts.text: Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. They that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly: their own personal gain. And by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple. If you are not studying, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody. It is warning you about fair speeches deceiving the hearts of the simple.

But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
Paul was warning, lest any man beguile you, deceive you, trick you. So he says in Romans: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly”: their own personal gain. They feed their own belly, their own mind.

Here is how they do it: “and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and lovely, beautiful speeches. If you ain't studying, especially you sisters, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody, and he's white. The scripture is warning you about fair speeches that deceive the hearts of the simple. Mark them and avoid them.

precepts.text: The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them. You will not find scriptures where the righteous seduce; the wicked always seduce the righteous. This is why brothers and sisters meet somebody in the world and convince themselves they can win them over. That never happens. It is not what the Bible says.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
Who beguiles whom? Proverbs says: “The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” Although the righteous is more excellent than his neighbor, the wicked seduce them.

You will not find scriptures where the righteous seduce, because seduce is a word with a negative meaning. The wicked always seduce the righteous, not the other way around.

This is why brothers and sisters meet somebody in the world and convince themselves, because he or she is so good-looking: I can win them over. I think I can win him; I think I can win her. That never happens; it is not what the Bible says. Just give it time, and you'll be out. Enticing words flow from the wicked to the righteous, never back.

precepts.text: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers, because they will seduce you. What fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? What communion hath light with darkness? What concord hath Christ with Belial? There is no agreement there. An infidel is an unbeliever, an idol worshipper. You think you have the Midas touch and can win them over; you are fooling yourself.

But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers”. Why? Because they will seduce you to serving Satan once again. But you'll say, no, he's so fine, so divine, I could win him; or, she's so lovely, I could win her over to this truth.

“for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?” What agreement has righteousness with unrighteousness? “and what communion hath light with darkness?” There is no agreement there. “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?”

An infidel is an idol worshipper, an unbeliever. You think you've got the Midas touch and can win them over; you are fooling yourself. Being yoked to the unbeliever is how the enticing words get to you, which is exactly what Colossians warns against.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, go tell him his fault between thee and him alone; then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established; and if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. This is for major things, not petty complaints. Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not deal with them, and the heathen were the other nations. Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you, and they always keep a little way back into your life, with fair speeches and kind words, to win you over to Satan.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
When we are warned not to be beguiled, and to avoid them that cause division, it is so that you and I don't get seduced: but he or she was my friend, I think I can win them back. No. Stop it. Christ laid out the order: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is for major things. It's not about stupidity like somebody moving your pencil from the right side of the table to the left, or a sister wanting people thrown out of the school because nobody likes her unleavened bread. You can't cook? Learn. We aren't throwing anybody out over your bread.

“And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not like them and did not talk with them. The heathen were the other nations. So deal with him like that. You don't know better than Christ.

Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you. They always keep a little way to get back into your life, a little hot pocket, to win you over to Satan with fair speeches and kind words: I always liked you, you were my favorite deacon, come over for dinner tonight, you're different than the rest of them. All that is to seduce you.

precepts.text: I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: which is not another. Why does it say which is not another? Because the Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people that Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. They were using the same text, but lying with deceitful words. There be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ: that is what the Christian church does today. That is their livelihood.

But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.

Family members and preachers who say come out of that Bible will seduce you right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and Pharisees were doing and what the Christian preachers do. Paul says: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”.

Why does it say which is not another? Because the Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice; they said salvation comes through sacrifice. That was the context Paul was dealing with. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people into believing Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. Same text, but lying with deceitful words.

“but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” That is what the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian church does today. They pervert the gospel of Christ; that is their livelihood.

We don't break up families. If your family has no issue with you in the scriptures and isn't trying to manipulate your children, fine. But if your family says, to hell with that Bible, let's smoke some weed and do what we used to do, you had better separate from them. All we can do is warn you.

precepts.text: Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you. We always skip that part: known among your tribes. Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise. So he took the chief of the tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over the people: captains over thousands, captains over hundreds, captains over fifties, captains over tens, and officers among the tribes. We are not making this structure up.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
Paul was not there in Laodicea, yet he was with them in spirit, “joying and beholding your order”. God loves order, and the order of Israel is written: “Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.”

We always skip that part: “known among your tribes.” Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. That is not something done to them; they decided to hide and be known only locally, and made themselves a nobody. How will we know you are wise and understanding? No brother has been held back from teaching the morning daily bread. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise: this brother is good, I listen to his classes, he travels, he's here one week and there another month.

“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do. So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” So we are not making this structure up. The captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens are in the law.

That is why IUIC is restructuring. Some men have positions and don't fit the bill: authority without wisdom, no knowledge, not knowing how to build men. The scripture calls for wise men, understanding, and known.

precepts.text: God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy, because all men have different gifts. Helps and governments go back to the stewardship program; it all falls into place.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
The order Moses set in the camp continues in the church: “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.”

The first leadership in the church is apostles, then prophets, then teachers. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy 1, because all men have different gifts. The wise and known men set over the tribes, and the apostles, prophets and teachers set in the church, are the same God's order.

“helps, governments, diversities of tongues”: that goes back to the stewardship program. It all falls into place. Every man has his gift and his place, and that structure is the order Paul rejoiced to behold in Colossians 2:5.

precepts.text: Set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city. Those elders go back to Deuteronomy 1:13-15: known men, wise amongst the people. When you hear people say rank is nothing: rank is important for structure's sake.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
Paul left Titus with a charge: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.” Set in order the things that are lacking.

Those elders go back to Deuteronomy 1:13-15 and to 1 Corinthians 12:28: known men, wise amongst the people, ordained in every city. Paul beheld order in Colossae and commanded order in Crete.

So when you hear people say rank ain't nothing: rank is important for structure's sake. The elders were appointed and set in order, and the body of Christ runs on that structure.

precepts.text: Let me not accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man; for in so doing my maker would soon take me away. Accepting a man's person is partiality. We have noticed in some sanctuaries that brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them, while passing over the man with wisdom in the scriptures and skills, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting them. A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom made a high ranking officer is just a flattering title. Job said God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say. You want men around you that will tell you when you are wrong; if everything you say is right, you are setting yourself up for a fall. If you are the smartest one in the room, you better find another room.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” Accepting a man's person is partiality. In some IUIC sanctuaries, brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them and like them. That is not scriptural. A man with wisdom in the scriptures, with skills, who knows how to deal with the people, gets passed over for the guy who kisses your behind.

A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom, made a captain or a high ranking officer: that's just a flattering title. He don't fit the bill. Officers of fifty, sixty, ten and twenty were asked to paraphrase Genesis on Abraham, father of many nations, and none of them could break it down. How did they get these titles?

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say: I like this friend better than the one that fits the bill, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting me. You want men like that around you. No dummies, no yes-men. If I say or do something wrong, I expect the men around me to say, Bishop, don't say that, don't do that.

When everything you say is right, you're a fool, setting yourself up for a fall. If you're the smartest one in the room, you better get out of the room and surround yourself with brothers that got some sense. That is order: men placed by what the scriptures say, not by flattery.

precepts.text: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. When difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching. That is called a hypocrite. You can only find that out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery, or hatred.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
Part of assessing a man for order is integrity: his actions in private compared to his words. “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” He teaches many, but when difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching.

That is called a hypocrite. And you can only find it out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery or hatred. That is why the assessment looks at how a man lives, not only how he talks: his honesty, his responsibility, his family, his finances, how he handles conflict.

A man set in authority has to profit himself with what he teaches. Paul joyed in beholding their order and the stedfastness of their faith; a teacher who is unprofitable to himself does not fit the bill, however much he knows.

precepts.text: Philip heard the eunuch read the prophet Esaias and said, understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, how can I, except some man should guide me? You get people that say just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.
precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught.” We must be rooted in Christ, and to be rooted you have to be studying; and if you are studying, you had better be applying, because you will be tested. A brother tells another brother to do what the scriptures say, and that brother gets mad and leaves because he is being pressured to do God’s work. That is simple.

“As ye have been taught”: the faith comes by being taught. Acts shows it: “And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.”

The eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah and could not understand it without a man to guide him. There are people who say, just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them. Being established in the faith comes by being taught, as the eunuch was taught by Philip.

precepts.text: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments. The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; the books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel. Paul was always studying. He was a man of study; he did not stop.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.
precepts.why:
To be “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith,” you have to study, and Paul is the example. “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.”

The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; he was going to be writing a lot of letters. The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel. Even in prison, Paul wanted his books.

Paul was always studying. He was a man of study, and he did not stop. We do four chapters a day; that is low level, but we have to start low level so we can get to a big level. Being rooted in Christ means never putting the books down.

precepts.text: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, that is soon to come.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.
precepts.why:
Colossians says to be stablished in the faith “as ye have been taught.” Hebrews says to remember those who taught you: “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.”

Those who have the rule over you are the ones who have taught you the word of God. Follow their faith, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, which is soon to come.

That also speaks to what happened with the old school. Some of the leadership went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs and throw it in the garbage? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Shake that dumb black mentality. Men make mistakes and men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby out with the bath water.

precepts.text: But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith. The key is yourselves. We can go over scriptures until we are blue in the face, but it is up to you to build up yourself, to study and apply. Study, pray, apply: that is upon every man and every woman. It is like the gym: the weights are there, put them to use. Likewise with the word of God.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.
precepts.why:
Colossians says “Rooted and built up in him.” Jude says who does the building: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.”

The key is yourselves. We can go over scriptures until we are blue in the face, but it is up to you to build yourself up, to study and apply. Study, pray, apply. That is upon every man and every woman; we cannot do it for you.

It is like going to the gym. Deacon Abiel goes twice a day, but if he just sat there and ate a sandwich he would not be building himself up; he would come back a Teletubby all over again. The weights are there; put them to use. Likewise with the word of God. Everybody has a Bible, everybody has the app. Study it, pray on it and apply it, and you will be rooted and built up in him and stablished in the faith.

precepts.text: The scribes and Pharisees asked why the disciples transgress the tradition of the elders, the oral traditions passed down, such as washing from fingertip to elbow before eating bread. Christ answered, why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? God commanded, honour thy father and mother; but they had a tradition where a child could say it is a gift, and be free from obeying his parents, like emancipation today. Thus they made the commandment of God of none effect: they were following traditions that contradicted God's laws.
precepts.point: Get your history right when you teach it: William Miller did not create the Seventh Day Adventists, he created the Millerites; it was Ellen G. White. Give the right breakdowns, or one day the enemy will catch you on it and embarrass you.
precepts.why:
“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men”. To see what the tradition of men does, go to the scribes and Pharisees.

“Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” The tradition of the elders means oral traditions passed down. They had a tradition that you had to wash your hands from the tip of the finger up to the elbow before you would eat.

Here is his answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” That is the fifth commandment, honour thy father and mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could declare himself a gift and be free from obeying his parents. It is what they call emancipation today: America has the same thing, get to sixteen and get away from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees were following traditions that contradicted God’s laws. That is the tradition of men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:8: whatever sets aside the commandment and is not after Christ.

precepts.text: And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death. That is what Christ was quoting.
precepts.point: Get your history right when you teach it: William Miller did not create the Seventh Day Adventists, he created the Millerites; it was Ellen G. White. Give the right breakdowns, or one day the enemy will catch you on it and embarrass you.
precepts.why:
When Christ said “He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”, he was quoting the law. Here is where he was getting it from: “And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.”

You curse your father and mother, you shall surely be put to death. But I’m mad at my father and mother, I’m going to curse him? Okay. Well, you are going to have a short life.

This is the commandment of God that the Pharisees made of none effect with their tradition of “It is a gift”. The law was plain, and the Son of God stood on it. That is what Colossians 2:8 means by beware of the tradition of men: the tradition of the elders set the child free from his parents, but the commandment of God says the one that curses them shall surely die.

precepts.text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, meaning your mind, and be no more stiffnecked, meaning hard headed. For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.
precepts.point: In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands: when we accept Christ as our king and savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. Let Christ's words circumcise our minds.
precepts.why:
“In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands.” The circumcision made without hands is explained in the law: “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” The foreskin of your heart means your mind, and stiffnecked means hard-headed.

To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. So Moses was already calling Israel to cut away what is in the mind, not only the flesh. “For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.” He is the God who requires it, and he regards no man's person.

So when we accept Christ as our king and our savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. Get rid of it. That is “putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ”: let Christ circumcise your mind. His words must circumcise our minds.

precepts.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts: that is how you know your heart is your mind, because evil thoughts do not come from the middle of your chest. Adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: all these evil things come from within, and defile the man. Definition read in class: lascivious describes someone or something driven by or tending to arouse unrestrained sexual desire; pornography falls under that.
precepts.point: In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands: when we accept Christ as our king and savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. Let Christ's words circumcise our minds.
precepts.why:
Why must we circumcise the heart? What's in it? Christ says: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” That is how you know your heart is your mind. Your evil thoughts don't come from the middle of your chest; they come from your mind, your thoughts.

Then the list: “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.” Lasciviousness describes someone or something driven by, or tending to arouse, unrestrained sexual desire: indecent, lewd or lustful behavior, thoughts or expressions. Pornography is one of them; you could throw that word right in there. An evil eye is when you hate your neighbor.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That's what defiles us, all of us. So this is what is cut off in the circumcision made without hands: all these immoralities in the mind, put off “by the circumcision of Christ.”

precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil. Once you got water baptized, you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings. The church has not figured that out; they think there is power in the water itself, but if nothing changes in you, you just went in wet and came out wet.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.
precepts.why:
“Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him.” Baptism was always symbolic. Isaiah says what the washing was for: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.”

So by water baptism, wash you, make you clean, put away the evil of your doings. Once you were water baptized, you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings. You are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature. That is the symbolism behind it.

“Cease to do evil.” The church has not figured that out yet. The Christian church thinks there is power in the water itself, that when you come out of the water you will no longer be a crackhead or a homosexual. No: if nothing changes in you, you went in and you came out wet. That is all. The change is in putting away the evil of your doings, not in the water.

precepts.text: The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us: not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, which is the water we read about in Isaiah 1:16, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Jesus Christ. A good conscience toward God means keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ. If you are living in sin when the Lord comes, you will not have a good conscience, and it comes out in your countenance.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.
precepts.why:
Water baptism keeps coming up over and over, and this is the verse they use: “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us.” They say, got you, baptism does save you. But watch the breakdown.

“Not the putting away of the filth of the flesh.” That is the water, the washing we read of in Isaiah 1:16. Peter makes it clear that the water does not save you. What saves is “the answer of a good conscience toward God”, and that comes “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ”.

A good conscience toward God is keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ. If you are a thief, a liar or a child molester when the Lord comes, you will not have a good conscience, and it comes out in your facial expressions. You will not make eye contact; your head is down, because you know there is something troubling you within. That is why Colossians says we are buried with him and “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God”: it is the faith and the changed life, not the water.

precepts.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. The old man is dead; whatever you were, it is passed away. This is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman; it is not mandatory, but it is an example.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.
precepts.why:
Colossians says we are “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.” Christ came up from the dead, and he is our example, to be like him. “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.” Why? Because you were buried in baptism. The old man is dead. The old woman is dead. The old hoe is dead.

“Old things are passed away.” All the old things you did, whether you were a crackhead, a meth head, an opium user, a fentanyl user, whatever it was, now you clean your system out. For anyone struggling with drugs, there is nothing wrong with getting clinical help; do not sit at home knowing the drug is there and that you are going to use it. There are clinics set up for that. If there are brothers or sisters trained in that field, maybe something can be set up so everything is done legitimately and lawfully. Until then, get the help you need.

“Behold, all things are become new.” This is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman. It is not mandatory, but it is an example. Water baptism was always a symbol of that same thing: the new man and the new woman coming up from the grave as a new person.

precepts.text: The first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us.” What ordinances? The subject has not changed: the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, saying salvation comes through sacrifice. Hebrews shows where those ordinances belong: “Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.”

The ordinances of divine service, the offerings and the worldly sanctuary, belonged to the first covenant. They did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us. Those are the ordinances Christ took out of the way and nailed to his cross, and verse 10 of the same chapter tells what they stood in and how long they were to last.

precepts.text: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation: until the time of Christ, the time of transformation.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
The ordinances of the first covenant “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Meats and drinks are the meat offerings and drink offerings. Divers washings: remember Matthew 15, when they complained, your disciples don't wash their hands. That's what we're talking about.

“carnal ordinances, imposed on them”: forced on the Israelites. “until the time of reformation”: until the time of Christ. Reformation means the time of transformation, which is when Christ came.

That is the handwriting of ordinances in Colossians 2:14. They were imposed only until Christ, and he blotted them out, “which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.” Going back to them is going backward.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not: God did not want it any more. He taketh away the first covenant of animal sacrifice, that he may establish the second, the new covenant in Christ, by the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. The Pharisees would say it is in the law, you must do animal sacrifice, and they would neglect the scriptures pointing to Christ.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law.” God didn't want it no more. Mark “which are offered by the law”: the law does say to do it, and the Pharisees would use that and say, no, it's in the law, you must do animal sacrifice. They would neglect the descriptions of Christ in Isaiah 53, in Zechariah 9 of the king coming lowly, and in the Psalms.

“Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” He took away the first covenant of animal sacrifice, that he might establish the second covenant, the new covenant in Christ: “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So the scribes were ignoring that. They said, we're not dealing with that. But the offering of Christ's body once for all is what blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.text: For dogs have compassed me: that was the scribes, Pharisees, and Rome. The assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. That is the crucifixion, and they ignored it.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
The Pharisees ignored the scriptures that described the sacrifice of Christ. The Psalms foretold it: “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.”

The dogs that compassed him were the scribes, the Pharisees and Rome. “they pierced my hands and my feet”: meaning sacrificed, crucified, capital punishment. That is the cross that the handwriting of ordinances was nailed to.

They would ignore that and say, no, no, no, we ain't dealing with that, and keep pushing goats and lambs. But the piercing of his hands and feet was written, and it is the sacrifice that took the ordinances out of the way.

precepts.text: Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin. His soul, not a goat or a lamb; and they ignored that too.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin.” It pleased the Lord to bruise him, Christ. See that: his soul an offering for sin, not a goat or a lamb.

The scribes said, well, we're just going to ignore that; we're dealing with goats, lambs and oxen, and to hell with all that mumbo gumbo y'all coming with. But the prophet said the offering for sin would be his soul, and then “he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.”

That is why the ordinances of animal sacrifice could be blotted out. The offering for sin that Isaiah saw was Christ himself.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks, 490 years, are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins: meaning a major sacrifice would happen. To make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy: the Son of God.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”: 490 years determined upon the Israelites and upon Jerusalem, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins.” To make an end of sins means a major sacrifice would happen.

“and to make reconciliation for iniquity”: to bring back the twelve tribes. “and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy”: to anoint the Son of God.

They said, well, we're not dealing with that; we're dealing with lambs, goats and bulls. Everybody see the problem? Daniel foretold one sacrifice that would make an end of sins, and that is the forgiveness of “all trespasses” in Colossians 2:13.

precepts.text: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, and will put my words in his mouth. Whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him: meaning he will cut you off.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
Moses himself foretold Christ: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” That Prophet is Christ.

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” Meaning he'll kill you; he'll cut you off. That is what the Lord is saying.

So those who held on to animal sacrifice and refused the words of Christ were refusing the very Prophet Moses spoke of. The law they claimed to defend told them to hearken to him, and he is the one who blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.text: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect. It could not make you perfect, because it was an animal. Christ is the perfection of that law; they refused to accept and understand that.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
Certain sins called for certain sacrifices, and all of that was against us, because it could not make us perfect: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience.”

It couldn't make you that did the service perfect, the priest or the one giving the offering. Why? It was an animal: a goat, a lamb, an ox or a turtledove. It was only a figure for that time.

Christ is the perfection of that law. They refused to accept and understand that, and that's the initial problem Paul was dealing with in Colossians 2. That is why the handwriting of ordinances “was contrary to us”, and why he “took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

precepts.text: Through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: and by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. There were sins that had no sacrifice under Moses, like witchcraft: the penalty was death. But under Christ, all that believe are justified from all things.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins.” You get forgiveness of sins through this man, Christ. “And by him all that believe are justified from all things”: justified, forgiven, from all things.

Like what? Witchcraft, homosexuality. Using drugs falls under witchcraft: I smoke weed, it open my mind, I see yonder soul. That's a demon. There was no ox or lamb for witchcraft; under Moses you died. Suffer not a witch to live: kill them. But under Christ, all that believe are justified from all things, “from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

The blood of bulls, goats, oxen and sheep could not give forgiveness for certain sins. That is what “having forgiven you all trespasses” means in Colossians 2:13: when we come into this truth, everything we have done is forgiven. A new slate.

precepts.text: God raised him from the dead and set him at his own right hand, far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come. Not only does he have a name above everything now, he is going to have a name above every name even in the world to come. And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, which is his body.
precepts.point: And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it. When he resurrected from the dead, he overcame all death, and everybody saw it: over five hundred people saw Christ at one time.
precepts.why:
Ephesians explains how Christ “spoiled principalities and powers”: it is the power “Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come.”

Why is that so heavy? Everybody argues about the name. Not only does Christ have a name above everything now; even in the world to come he is going to have a name above every name. Nobody is going to have his name. You have a million men named Jesus running through Puerto Rico; who is that?

“And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.” Christ is the head over all things to the church, and the church is his body.

So back in Colossians: he was not supposed to come back, but with the power of God, being the creator, he rose from the dead and overcame all death. “He made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.” Everybody saw him come from the grave; over five hundred people saw Christ at one time. That is the triumph over the principalities and powers, and it sets him far above every one of them.

precepts.text: Who was going around judging people? The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: they were the judges. All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders. Imagine a poor brother with a sin needing forgiveness, told he must bring a bull he cannot afford. That is how they rolled, because they wanted that money.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink”. Wait: who was going around judging people? Christ tells us: “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat in Moses’ seat, meaning they were the judges.

“All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites. “For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.”

Imagine you are a poor brother with a sin you want forgiveness for, and they tell you that you have to get a bull. You say, I cannot afford a bull; I have two sheep over here. Well, that is too damn bad. That is how these dudes rolled, because they wanted that money.

So the men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:16 are these judges, the ones laying the burden of the sacrifices on the people after Christ had come.

precepts.text: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? The master is Christ. One man esteemeth one day above another: the Jews that followed Moses esteemed the day through sacrifice. Another esteemeth every day alike: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices; they accepted what Christ did. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind: fully persuaded that Christ's sacrifice absolves you of sin. There was a dispensation of time from the crucifixion until the temple fell where people were still struggling to accept that; it is not talking about being fully persuaded on whether to keep God's laws. He that regardeth the day through sacrifice regardeth it unto the Lord, and he that regardeth not the day, because he accepted Christ, to the Lord he doth not regard it. For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
Here is another precept about them judging people: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” Remember who the master is: the master is Christ.

“One man esteemeth one day above another”. How did they esteem it? Through sacrifice: on the sabbath day you had to offer two lambs of the first year. The Jews that were following Moses esteemed one day above another through sacrifice. “another esteemeth every day alike”: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices. They said, we are just going to accept what Christ did; we are not doing burnt offerings. Like today: here is the sabbath day, and we are not esteeming it with animal sacrifice.

“Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” Fully persuaded in Christ: that his sacrifice, his dying for you, forgives your sins. There was a dispensation of time from the time he was crucified until the temple fell, when people went back to the temple and were still struggling to accept that Christ coming to die would absolve them of sin, and they were given time to be fully persuaded. It is not being fully persuaded about keeping the laws of God, like adultery. No.

“He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord”: regarding it through sacrifice. “and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it”, because he accepted Christ and did not need the goats and the bulls. “He that eateth, eateth to the Lord”: eating the animal sacrifice, you eat to the Lord and give God thanks, and he that eats not gives God thanks as well. “For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.” “For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.”

precepts.text: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin. Some ate of the sacrifices but were not fully persuaded at this point.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
“And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.”

There were some who doubted that Christ’s blood was able to absolve them of their sins, and they ate of the sacrifices. Some ate, but they were not fully persuaded at this point. That is the doubt Paul is talking about.

People say fully persuaded means, I am not fully clear that eating pork is wrong, because of the New Testament. That is not what it is talking about. It is being persuaded that Christ’s blood would absolve them from sin. So the eating in Romans 14, like the meat of Colossians 2:16, is the eating of the sacrifices, not the eating of unclean meat.

precepts.text: This is how you esteemed the day. On the sabbath day, two lambs of the first year without spot, with the meat offering of flour mingled with oil and the drink offering thereof: this is the burnt offering of every sabbath. In the beginnings of your months, the new moon: two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot, with their meat offerings and drink offerings measured out in hins of wine, and one kid of the goats for a sin offering. This is what the Pharisees were judging the people on.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
This is how you esteemed the day, and this is what the Pharisees were judging the people on. “And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof:” “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath”. Two lambs that are one year old: that is how you esteemed the sabbath.

Now watch the new moon: “in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot”. Two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs on a new moon, one year old, without blemish. The meat offering was flour “mingled with oil”, measured for each bullock, each ram and each lamb, “for a burnt offering of a sweet savour, a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.”

“And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb”. There was a measuring instrument you had to use to measure the wine; the drink offerings were men pouring out wine. “this is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.” “And one kid of the goats for a sin offering”.
