So “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days” is meat offerings and drink offerings: on certain high holy days so many lambs or goats, on the new moon the bullocks, ram and seven lambs, on the sabbath the meat and drink offerings. Do not let a Christian use that verse to say it is talking about pork and getting drunk. That is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said. And they “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

precepts.text: Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: some of them hath he made high days and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
“Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?” “By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.” “Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

The same sun lights every day, but the Lord made some days high days and hallowed them. That is one man esteeming one day above another. What the Lord did back then to esteem the sabbath was two lambs a year old offered on that day.

Then Christ came and fulfilled that, and the Pharisees said, hell no; go back to that lamb, go back to that goat. That is what they were doing, judging the people in respect of the holyday, the new moon and the sabbath for not bringing the sacrifices that esteemed those days.

precepts.text: It shall be the prince's part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. The meat and drink of Colossians 2:16 are these offerings.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
Christians use the meat in Colossians 2:16 to say you can eat pork, and the drink to say you can get drunk. It is not talking about that. Stop listening to these dumb Christians, especially if they are black or Latino; never listen to them.

Ezekiel explains it: “And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”. See that: meat offerings, drink offerings, in the feasts, the new moons and the sabbaths, the very same list as Colossians 2:16.

“he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” These offerings were made for reconciliation. So Paul’s words read: let no man judge you in meat offerings, or in drink offerings, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, because the reconciliation those offerings pointed to is in Christ.

precepts.text: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. It was temporary.
precepts.point: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come.
precepts.why:
Colossians says the meats, drinks, holy days, new moons and sabbaths the people were being judged by “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come. Hebrews says it the same way: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

The law of sacrifice was a shadow of things to come, which was Christ. It was not the very image. Those sacrifices offered year after year could never make the people perfect. It was temporary.

That is why the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling the people when they said, go back to the lamb, go back to the goat. The Sabbath had once been esteemed with two lambs of the first year; Christ came and fulfilled that. The shadow pointed to him, and the body is of Christ.

precepts.text: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: see that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount. Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens.
precepts.point: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come.
precepts.why:
The priests under the law were those “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens. The tabernacle, the service and the sacrifices were made after a pattern shown to him in the mount; they were an example and a shadow, not the heavenly things themselves.

That is what Colossians means: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The service Moses set up was a pattern pointing to the real thing, and the real thing is Christ. So no man should judge you or beguile you back into the shadow when the body has come.

precepts.text: My temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus. You see how men are received like angels.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”. What does he mean by worshipping of angels? Paul shows it: “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.”

The Galatians received Paul, a man, as an angel of God. You see how men are considered like angels. So the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18 is the worshipping of men: following man, voluntarily humbling yourself to men.

And he is not changing the subject. It goes back to verse 4, “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words”, and verse 8, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” He is on the same train of thought, repeating it again.

So when you read verse 18, it is not Michael and Uriel coming down from the heavens to talk to you. It is men that speak so well, with enticing words and the wisdom of this world, received as if they were angels of God, and people giving themselves over to them.

precepts.text: Behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be. Do not let anybody trick you out of your reward.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“Let no man beguile you of your reward”. What reward? Christ says: “And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.”

Christ comes quickly, and his reward is with him, to give every man of the children of Israel according as his work shall be. That is the reward Paul is guarding in Colossians 2:18.

To beguile is to deceive, to trick. So “Let no man beguile you of your reward” means: don't let nobody trick you out of getting your reward in Christ. The men with enticing words and bright ideas are not only leading you astray in doctrine; they are robbing you of what Christ is bringing with him when he comes. Your work is what the reward answers to, so don't let a man turn your work away from Christ.

precepts.text: Without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
The reward of Colossians 2:18 is for those who come to God by faith: “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

God is a rewarder, and he rewards those that diligently seek him. Christ said his reward is with him “to give every man according as his work shall be”, and here we see it is faith that pleases him and diligent seeking that he rewards.

So when Paul says “Let no man beguile you of your reward”, this is what is at stake. The men beguiling the believers were turning them away from faith in Christ, back to the carnal ordinances, putting Moses over Christ and animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ. Without faith it is impossible to please God, so a man who talks you out of your faith in Christ is talking you out of your reward.

precepts.text: The counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God. That is how speaking with Ahithophel was regarded: like the word of God came from heaven. That is the sense of receiving a man as an angel; it is not Michael and Uriel coming down from the heavens to talk to you.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.”

That is how speaking with Ahithophel was regarded: as if you enquired at an angel of God, like the word of God came from heaven. Ahithophel was a man, but his counsel was received like an oracle, both by David and by Absalom.

That is the sense of the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18. You thought Michael and Uriel came from the heavens to talk to you? That is not what it means. It is the worshipping of men that speak so well, with enticing words, with the wisdom of this world. Paul spoke of “the wisdom of this world” and “the princes of this world, that come to nought”. It goes into the same thing.

So “a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels” is you voluntarily humbling yourself in the worshipping of man: receiving a man's word as if it were an oracle of God, the way they did with Ahithophel. Let no man beguile you of your reward that way.

precepts.text: We do not cease to pray for you, that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; that ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God. That is how you are not beguiled.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
How do you go about not being beguiled? Paul answered it in the first chapter: “For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding”.

“That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;” “Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness”.

That's how you are not beguiled: filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, increasing in the knowledge of God. If you study, you don't willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Paul said it too: study to show thyself approved, so that you will be able to withstand these men coming in and beguiling you.

The “voluntary humility” of Colossians 2:18 is people giving themselves over willingly. The cure is knowledge. A believer filled with the knowledge of God's will is not left to humble himself to a man with enticing words.

precepts.text: Many of the Jews which had seen the things which Jesus did believed on him: they saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead. But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done. You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God. Those same evil spirits are around today.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
Here is another example of the evil of these people: “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead.

But watch the next verse: “But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God: I'm going to tell the scribes and Pharisees what Christ done did.

If I saw Christ raise somebody, I'm at his hip. I'm not leaving his side. I'm with him forever. I'm not running to them down yonder.

Them people back then, those same evil spirits are around today. Some see the truth with their own eyes and still go running to the men they have made their heads, the scribes and Pharisees, instead of holding to Christ. That is the voluntary humility and worshipping of men in Colossians 2:18: giving yourself over to men who are enemies of God, and being beguiled of your reward.

precepts.text: Certain men from Judaea taught the brethren, except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, and went up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles, the diaspora. But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses: not only circumcision, but back to animal sacrifice. This is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up: the bright idea that they had to do all those sacrifices of Numbers 28 or they could not be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles?
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,” “And not holding the Head”. Who's the head? Christ. What were they intruding into? Acts 15 is an example.

“And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” If you ain't circumcised, you don't get salvation. “When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.”

They passed through Phenice and Samaria, “declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, the diaspora, “and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.” At Jerusalem “they declared all things that God had done with them.”

Then here it comes: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” Which believed: they said they accepted Christ. But they wanted them to go back to the animal sacrifice, not only get circumcised.

That is the bright idea. These negros have bright ideas: reading the scriptures on their own, the light bulb over the head, telling people they don't need nobody. They looked in the scriptures and said you got to do all those sacrifices of Numbers 28 or else you can't be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles? That is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up by a fleshly mind, and not holding the Head.

precepts.text: Certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment. The apostles said that order did not come from us. It seemed good to send chosen men with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
The apostles answered those Pharisees: “Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law”. Troubled you with words, subverting your souls: getting you away from Christ. Keep the law here is the law of animal sacrifice.

“to whom we gave no such commandment”. Hear what the apostles said: we didn't give that order; that didn't come from us. “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,” “Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

So you see the problem. Christ was dealing with the apostles, and Christ never told the apostles they had to get circumcised and deal with animal sacrifice. But these Pharisees that believed looked in the scriptures and put their bright ideas to them.

That is “vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind” in Colossians 2:18: I'm the priest, I understand it, not you apostles. And it is “not holding the Head”. The men who came from Judea went out from the apostles without their commandment, and the believers were beguiled by words the apostles never gave.

precepts.text: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ. These men were not holding Christ as the head.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“And not holding the Head”: who is the Head? “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ”. Christ is the head.

These men were not holding Christ as the head. They were putting Moses over Christ, animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

Then Colossians 2:19 goes on: “from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered”. We are the body of Christ; we get our understanding, we are nourished through Christ. Follow what Christ said and we are going to be okay. “and knit together”, like we read in Judges 20 about being knit together as one man: honoring one another, preferring one another. “increaseth with the increase of God”: one man plants, another man waters, but it is God that gives the increase, and he is doing so.

So to hold the Head is to grow up into Christ in all things. Letting a man beguile you back to the ordinances is letting go of the Head the whole body is nourished from.

precepts.text: The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered. You had to eat these offerings; touch, taste, and handle belong to that service.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.
precepts.why:
Paul asks, “why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances, (Touch not; taste not; handle not”. Why are you going back to those ordinances? He has not changed the subject since verse 14, “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us”, and those ordinances are the “carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation” of Hebrews 9:10: until the time of Christ.

Leviticus shows what touch, taste and handle belong to: “the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning. But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten”. You had to eat these offerings. Eating, eating: that is the touching, tasting and handling of the sacrifice.

So when Colossians 2:21 says “Touch not; taste not; handle not”, it is saying leave it alone. The men beguiling the believers were rejecting Christ, saying the animal is above Christ: you need that goat, you need that lamb, that ram, that ox, that bull. Paul was saying no, Christ is above all. He taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary, and his sacrifice is supreme.

precepts.text: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.
precepts.why:
Colossians 2:22 says the ordinances “Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men” Christ said the same of the scribes and Pharisees: “But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

That is why Paul calls the call back to the sacrifices the commandments and doctrines of men. Christ had come and taught the perfect way. Anyone still pushing the believers back under those carnal ordinances was teaching men’s commandments as doctrine, and that worship is in vain.

So stop following man. The ordinances of touch not, taste not, handle not were temporary and perish with the using; going back to them after Christ is worshipping in vain.

precepts.text: Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. Paul repeats himself: if any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.
precepts.why:
Paul already said how serious it is to bring another doctrine: “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” They were coming with a different doctrine than Christ, so let him be accursed.

Then he repeats himself so nobody misses it: “As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.”

That is the weight behind Colossians 2:22. The men teaching the believers to go back to animal sacrifice after Christ were preaching another gospel than the one they had received, and whether it is a man or an angel from heaven, the one who brings it is accursed.

precepts.text: Moses truly said, a prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things. And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people. You reject Christ and what he said, that is your outcome. This is what Paul was warning them about.
precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.
precepts.why:
“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me”. Peter is getting this from Deuteronomy 18:15 to 19, and that prophet is Christ.

“him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.” Hear him in how many things? All things. “And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.” You reject Christ, you reject what he said, and that is your outcome.

This is what Paul was warning the Colossians about. The men beguiling them were trying to trick and deceive the followers of Christ into going back to the carnal ordinances of animal sacrifice: get that lamb, get that ram, get that goat, get that ox. Christ taught that his sacrifice is supreme, and every soul that will not hear him on it shall be destroyed from among the people.

precepts.text: On the day of atonement ye shall afflict your souls: fasting, no eating and no drinking for the entire day, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.
precepts.why:
Colossians 2:23 speaks of “will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body”. That goes back to verse 18, “in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”: Paul has not changed the subject. Will worship is voluntary worship of what men say, humility here is humbling yourself to man, and neglecting of the body deals with fasting.

Leviticus shows the fast: “Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” The tenth day of the seventh month is the day of atonement. To afflict your souls means to fast: no eating and no drinking for the entire 24-hour day.

And on that day you had to do what? Offer an offering made by fire. The fast and the sacrifice went together under the law. That is the “shew of wisdom” in Colossians 2:23: it has a show of wisdom because it is in the scriptures. It is there, but the sacrifice part of it was temporary.

precepts.text: Sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past. The margin note points that fast to the tenth day of the seventh month, Leviticus 23:27. Paul kept the day of atonement, but was he sacrificing on the day? No, because he had faith in Christ.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.
precepts.why:
“Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them”. The margin note beside “the fast” points it to the tenth day of the seventh month, Leviticus 23:27 and 29: the day of atonement.

So Paul kept the day of atonement. But was Paul sacrificing on that day? No. Why? Because he had that faith in Christ. He fasted, but he was not offering an animal on that day.

That is the line Colossians 2:23 draws. Neglecting of the body, the fasting, is not the problem; Paul kept the fast himself. The problem is the men who used a show of wisdom to pull the believers back under the carnal ordinances of sacrifice after Christ had come.

precepts.text: For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts. Fasting was meant to curb the desires; not with these men.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.
precepts.why:
The end of Colossians 2:23, “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh”, seems like hard wording. Other translations read it, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying and sacrificing, and they were still sexually indulgent all over the place: spiritual discipline, worldly desires, spiritual discipline, temptation, over and over.

Timothy describes that same sort: “For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts”. He is talking about these scribes and Pharisees, these type of men.

I thought fasting was meant to curb your desires. Not with these men. It inflamed their desires. They showed humility and neglected the body with fasting, and they still crept into houses to lead silly women captive. That is what Paul means by no honour to the satisfying of the flesh.

precepts.text: There are certain men crept in unawares, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. Everything in the Bible with them turned into sexual immorality. Those spirits are back today.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.
precepts.why:
When it came to satisfying the flesh, these men had no honour. No honour. Jude names them: “For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Lasciviousness means sexual immorality. They turned the grace of God into it, and they denied the Father and the Son. Everything in the Bible with them turned out to be some sex: I could get two wives, three wives, four wives. This woman make me mad, I got two more women over there I’mma deal with, then I’mma take your money and you buy me a Maserati. The hell is this? These dudes are wicked as hell.

Those spirits are back today. That is why Paul warns about a show of wisdom in will worship and humility and neglecting of the body that is not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: men who look religious and fast, but whose god is sex.

precepts.text: Not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
The body is one and has many members, “so also is Christ.” Another brother brought Colossians: “And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” It takes some explaining, but it speaks to the same thing.

The body is held together from the Head, Christ. From him the whole body, joined and banded together, has nourishment ministered to it and is knit together, and so it increases with the increase of God. The members do not hold themselves together; they are knit together by holding the Head.

That is the unity of the body: every joint and band ministering what it has been given, all fastened to the Head. Not holding the Head is how a body falls apart, and holding him is how it grows. That is why the next scriptures read go straight to Christ as the head of the body, the church.

precepts.text: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men.
precepts.point: God polluted Israel with man-made religions founded in America after slavery.
precepts.why:
“I have polluted mine inheritance.” How did God pollute his people? With man-made religions. Paul warns: “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” None of these religions are after Christ.

Look at where they came from. Pope Nicholas V, the father of the transatlantic slave trade, and after the popes the Protestants. John Smith created the Baptist religion. Joseph Smith created the Mormon religion in 1830. Ellen G. White created the Seventh-day Adventist religion in 1863. Charles T. Russell created the Jehovah's Witness religion in 1872. Charles Parham created the Pentecostal religion in 1901.

These run from slavery up to 1863, when we so-called got emancipated, and on through Jim Crow and segregation. The same people who held us as slaves handed us these religions. What happened to John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 while our people were in chains? They took that out of the Bible at that time.

So Isaiah 47:6 shows God allowed us to be polluted: “I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand.” The traditions of men that spoiled our people are part of that pollution, and that is why Christ is the enemy of Christianity.

precepts.text: They encourage themselves in an evil matter; they commune of laying snares privily.
precepts.point: The wicked search out iniquities from Babylon and the old mystic nations and spread them through music and advertising.
precepts.why:
“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world.” To spoil is to despoil and corrupt. It is a vain deceit because there is covetousness behind it, reward behind it, gifts. The rudiments are the elements of the world, of man. David shows who is behind those traditions: “They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?”

Who are they? Go up to verse 2: “Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.” The secret counsel of the wicked are the elite that sit back and research and study ancient pagan cultures and ancient Eastern cultures and incorporate them into our society today. Some call them Illuminati, some call them the Luciferians. It is all of them: Bilderbergs, Duponts, Rothschilds, whatever. An elite group that runs this world behind the scenes and builds the customs and societal norms we grew up in, that we believed were righteous and are not. And we reference the customs of these elite demons as if they were God himself.

They “commune of laying snares”: they communicate, have conversations, think tanks. The snares are doctrines, religions, philosophies, politics, laid privily for our people, who they know are the real people of God. “Who shall see them?” You do not know a Luciferian if you meet one; he has to tell you he is part of a secret society. They are known, but they are not known.

“They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search.” They search out iniquities from the ancient mystic civilisations: Babylon, Assyria, Rome, Greece, Canaan, the Sidonians, the Germanic cultures, Norse folklore. Their archaeologists do diligent searches and excavations, dig these things up, revamp them, commercialise them and make them appealing and alluring to the foolish and ignorant. And “both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.”

They have all kinds of slick ways: television, radio, propaganda, advertisement. That is their signs and wonders, and it is all witchcraft. They will get you one way or the other, through influence, music and fashion. Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer, Jingle Bells: you have to check yourself because it is catchy. That is the tradition of men Paul warned about, spoiling our people through the holidays.

precepts.text: The meat, drink, holydays, and sabbaths are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ; the Passover lamb was a precursor of him.
precepts.point: The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.
precepts.why:
“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. The lamb is a foreshadowing. “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

The feast days and the sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, and the body that casts the shadow is Christ. The Passover lamb taken on the tenth day, a lamb for an house, was a precursor of him. So the ordinance in Egypt is not only about a lamb; it is pointing forward to the one the lamb stands for.

precepts.text: Let no man judge you in meat, or in drink; Paul defended the congregations from those pushing them back to the sacrifices.
precepts.point: In our captivity, with no Levitical priesthood and no temple, keeping the commandments is the offering and the reasonable service: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and we present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. And Ezekiel 20 shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, offerings will be required again in the holy mountain.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
This is the context so much of Paul's letters sit in. “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days.”

Paul was convincing the congregations that they no longer had to sacrifice animals, because Pharisees were creeping in trying to turn them back to those things, the meat and drink of the offerings. Therefore let no man judge you in meat or in drink; Christ had already given himself as the offering and the sacrifice of a sweetsmelling savour.

precepts.text: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, nailing it to his cross; let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.
precepts.point: The law of sacrifice was contrary to us because those sacrifices offered year by year continually could never make the comers thereunto perfect. It was a scapegoat so the law would not have to kill us; the Most High has been extending grace since Adam, for he had every right to kill Adam and Eve, and instead extended grace through the animal sacrifice. If the law of sacrifice still stood, there would be no sacrifice for worshipping other gods, and we would be done as a people; it was taken out of the way so Israel could come back to God.
precepts.why:
“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross”. The handwriting of ordinances is the law of sacrifice listed in Leviticus 7:37.

“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” Add the word offering: the meat offering and drink offering we just read in Leviticus. No man can condemn you because you are not sacrificing animals any more, or for how you observe a holyday, new moon, or sabbath pertaining to sacrifice, for those are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.

precepts.text: Let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday; no man may condemn you for keeping the holy days without the sacrifices, now that Christ is come.
precepts.point: The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
With the two wave loaves came burnt offerings, a sin offering and peace offerings, “with their meat offering, and their drink offerings.” That is what Colossians is talking about: “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days.”

Those who did not believe in Christ condemned the followers of Christ as wicked for not sacrificing on the holy days. We still keep the holy days, but we do not offer the offerings, because the body of Christ has been given. No man may judge you for keeping the holyday without the meat and drink offerings, now that Christ is come.

precepts.text: The handwriting of ordinances against us was nailed to the cross; let no man judge you in meat, or in drink, or of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.
precepts.point: This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
The burnt offering of every sabbath is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest. “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The meat and drink offerings of the sabbath were a shadow of things to come, and the body is of Christ.

Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

precepts.text: Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels.
precepts.point: Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel told Manoah, “if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord.” He knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. “Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind”.

Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God, because we cannot see the Most High; that is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. Manoah did not even know he was an angel of the Lord, yet the angel turned the offering to the Lord before the error could be made.

precepts.text: That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love; the will of Christ for the church at Colosse, the same knitting of souls.
precepts.point: Address the perversion head on, as we did last class: souls being knit is not talking about anything unnatural between the two men. The same word describes the church: hearts knit together in love, as joints and bands in one body. Jonathan and David were on one accord; they had the same spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
In 1 Samuel 18, “the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.” Address the perversion head on: souls being knit is not talking about anything unnatural between the two men.

The same word describes the church. The will of Christ for the church at Colosse was “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ”. That is the same knitting of souls.

So when Jonathan and David “made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul”, and Jonathan gave David his robe, his garments, “even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle”, it was two brothers on one accord, with the same spirit.

precepts.text: The body, by joints and bands knit together, increaseth with the increase of God; as muscles and joints are knit into one body, so were Jonathan and David of one spirit.
precepts.point: Address the perversion head on, as we did last class: souls being knit is not talking about anything unnatural between the two men. The same word describes the church: hearts knit together in love, as joints and bands in one body. Jonathan and David were on one accord; they had the same spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
The body, “by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” As muscles and joints are knit into one body, so were Jonathan and David of one spirit.
